items.title: Section: The Seventh Aspect Opens and Closes — Rebirth as a Wheel-Turning King, and Constant, Correct Vows

items.zh: 又住於此，在在生處多作輪王，王贍部洲，得大自在。遠離一切所有慳垢，威被有情，調伏慳悋。諸四攝事所作業中，一切不離佛法僧寶，證一切種菩提作意。恒發願言：我當一切有情中尊，作諸有情一切義利所依止處。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: taking rebirth; first, most often becoming a wheel-turning king. Furthermore, dwelling in this abode, in whatever place of rebirth, one most often becomes a wheel-turning king, ruling Jambudvīpa, attaining great sovereignty. Entirely free of every stain of miserliness, overawing sentient beings with majesty, subduing one's own miserly stinginess.
Second, constantly making correct vows. In every undertaking belonging to the four means of attraction, never departing from the three jewels, accomplishing an intention fixed on every kind of awakening.
Commentary: Regarding "in every undertaking belonging to the four means of attraction" and the like — the bodily, verbal, and mental karma subsumed within the skilful means of the four means of attraction is called every undertaking belonging to the four means of attraction. Within all such undertakings, being mindful of the buddha, dharma, and sangha, abiding in great reverence, eliminating every deluded conceptual construction, dedicating everything done towards unsurpassed awakening — this is called never departing from the three jewels, accomplishing an intention fixed on every kind of awakening.
Constantly making this vow: I shall become most honoured among all sentient beings, becoming the very support on which every sentient being's own highest benefit depends.

items.title: Section: The Eighth and Final Aspect Opens — Majestic Power Through Diligence, Renouncing the Throne to Attain a Hundred Samādhis

items.zh: 若樂發起如是精進，棄捨一切家屬、財位，歸佛聖教，淨信出家。一剎那頃，瞬息須臾能證菩薩百三摩地。以淨天眼，能於種種諸佛國土見百如來。又即於彼變化住持、菩薩住持皆能解了。
items.en: Eighth aspect: majestic power; first, the power arising from diligence. Should one delight in arousing this very diligence, relinquishing every family member and every treasure and throne, taking refuge in the buddha's noble teaching, going forth with pure faith into monastic life — in an instant, in the blink of an eye, within a muhūrta, one is able to realise a hundred bodhisattva samādhis. With a pure divine eye, one is able to behold a hundred tathāgatas across every kind of buddha-land. And regarding what is sustained there through emanation and what is sustained for bodhisattvas — the emanation lands and the enjoyment lands — one is able to understand them completely.

items.title: Section: The Remaining Ten Attainments — Shaking a Hundred Worlds, a Hundred Bodies, Each With a Hundred Bodhisattva Retinues

items.zh: 以神通力動百世界，身亦能往。放大光明周匝遍照，普令他見。化為百類，成熟百種所化有情。若欲留命，能住百劫。於前後際各百劫事，智見能入。蘊、界、處等諸法門中，於百法門能正思擇。化作百身，身身皆能現百菩薩眷屬圍繞。
items.en:
With spiritual power, shaking a hundred world-systems, the body also able to go there. Emitting great light, illuminating all around, universally causing others to see. Transforming into a hundred kinds, bringing a hundred kinds of beings to be transformed to maturity. If wishing to prolong life, able to remain for a hundred eons. Regarding matters of a hundred eons in both past and future, wisdom and vision are able to penetrate them. Within the dharma-gateways of the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, and the rest, able to correctly discern a hundred such dharma-gateways. Transforming into a hundred bodies, each and every body able to display a retinue of a hundred bodhisattvas surrounding it.
Commentary: Regarding "the sustaining power of transformation, the sustaining power of bodhisattvas" — this means the transformation-land and the land of actual enjoyment, respectively, which should be understood in this order.

items.title: Section: Immeasurable Power From Vow-Force Alone — Closing the Eighth and Final Aspect Entirely

items.zh: 自茲以去，是諸菩薩由願力故，當知無量威力神變，安住如是極歡喜住諸菩薩眾願力增上，能引無量殊勝正願所作神變。如是正願，乃至俱胝那庾多百千大劫，不易可數。
items.en:
Second, the power arising from a correct vow. From this point onward, these bodhisattvas, by the power of their vow, should be understood to accomplish immeasurable majestic, spiritually transformative power. Bodhisattvas abiding in this abode of utmost joy, through the heightened power of their vows, are able to draw forth immeasurable, excellent, correct vows' own transformations. Such correct vows, continuing even across koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of great eons, become genuinely difficult to number.
Commentary: Regarding "by the power of their vow, immeasurable majestic, spiritually transformative power should be understood" — bodhisattvas, if by the sovereign, heightened power of their own vow, produce transformations that, in number, exceed everything enumerated before and cannot be counted, hence it is said to be immeasurable.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Eight Aspects Together — Closing the Brief Answer for the Abode of Utmost Joy

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩極歡喜住。謂善決定故，四相發心故，發起精進引發正願故，淨修住法故，開曉餘住故，修治善根故，受生故，威力故。
items.en: Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode of utmost joy — namely, because of a well-determined vow; because of the fourfold mark of arising bodhicitta; because of arousing diligence and giving rise to a correct vow; because of dharmas purifying the abode; because of being shown the way towards the remaining abodes; because of cultivating wholesome roots; because of taking rebirth; because of majestic power.

items.title: Section: Pointing to the Ten Grounds Sutra for Full Detail, and Explaining Why "Ground" and "Abode" Are Both Used — Closing the Entire Abode of Utmost Joy

items.zh: 若廣宣說，如十地經極喜地說。彼十地經廣所宣說菩薩十地，即是此中菩薩藏攝摩怛理迦略所宣說菩薩十住。如其次第，從極歡喜住，乃至最上成滿菩薩住。應知此中，由能攝持菩薩義故，說名為地；能為受用居處義故，說名為住。
items.en:
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to the corresponding account. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of utmost joy. What the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds at length as the bodhisattva's ten grounds is exactly what this text, subsumed within the bodhisattva canon's own root-matrix, expounds in brief as the bodhisattva's ten abodes. In their proper sequence, from the abode of utmost joy through the abode of ultimate accomplishment.
Second, explaining the terms ground and abode. One should understand that within this, because it is able to hold and sustain what belongs to a bodhisattva's own meaning, it is called a ground; because it serves as the dwelling-place one actually enjoys and makes use of, it is called an abode.

blocks.text: A short day. The first-ground bodhisattva's powers, described in hundreds, and the treatise refers you to the *Ten Grounds Sūtra* for the rest.

Venerable Miào Jìng: of the four kinds of wheel-turning king, this should be the iron-wheel king; he subdues the stinginess in his own mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: the iron-wheel king rules Jambudvīpa alone.

Master Cháng Bǎi: an instant is about 0.013 seconds; a xūyú is forty-eight minutes. Venerable Miào Jìng: "a hundred buddhas" means a hundred great trichiliocosms, since one world has only one buddha; having the pure divine eye means the first absorption has been attained.
"If wishing to prolong life, able to remain for a hundred eons." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva has mastery over lifespan.

"As the *Ten Grounds Sūtra* explains in its ground of utmost joy; its ten grounds are this text's ten abodes." Master Cháng Bǎi: "abode" emphasises dwelling; "ground" emphasises holding and growing the bodhisattva's merits.

The second part of the Bodhisattva Ground opened with the marks of a true bodhisattva and moved, through compassion and aspiration, to the first ground. It is the most hopeful fascicle so far: the fearful, inconsistent beginner of Day 418 becomes the joyful bodhisattva of today.

quiz.q: As a wheel-turning king, "subduing stinginess" — the English says subduing beings' stinginess. How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it, and which kind of king?
options: an iron-wheel king, subduing the stinginess in his own mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: of the four kinds of wheel-turning king, this should be the iron-wheel king; he subdues the stinginess in his own mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: the iron-wheel king rules Jambudvīpa alone.

quiz.q: "In an instant, a blink, a xūyú — a hundred samādhis." The English merges the three. How do the lectures distinguish them, and how read "emanation-sustaining, bodhisattva-sustaining"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: an instant ≈ 0.013 sec, a blink, a xūyú 48 minutes; Miào Jìng: emanation-sustaining is the emanated land (shared by ordinary and noble) — not the "sustaining power" in the English
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: an instant is about 0.013 seconds; a blink is the time of an eye-blink; a xūyú is 48 minutes. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "emanation" refers to the emanated land, shared by ordinary and noble beings. The English merges the three and renders the lands as "sustaining power."

quiz.q: "With the divine eye seeing a hundred tathāgatas." How does Venerable Miào Jìng reckon the worlds, and what absorption does the divine eye need?
options: one buddha per world, so a hundred great trichiliocosms; the pure divine eye implies at least the first absorption
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one world has only one buddha, so this means a hundred great trichiliocosms; having the pure divine eye means the first absorption has been attained.

quiz.q: Through the power of diligence, how long can the bodhisattva remain if wishing to prolong life?
quiz.why: "If wishing to prolong life, able to remain for a hundred eons." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva has mastery over lifespan.

quiz.q: For a fuller account of the abode of utmost joy, which sūtra does the treatise point to?
options: the Ten Grounds Sūtra, ground of utmost joy
quiz.why: "As the Ten Grounds Sūtra explains in its ground of utmost joy; its ten grounds are this text's ten abodes." Venerable Miào Jìng: mātṛkā is "root-mother" — it grows your wisdom.

quiz.q: "Called 'ground' because it holds the bodhisattva's meaning; 'abode' because it is a dwelling to enjoy." How do the lectures develop this?
options: Cháng Bǎi: "abode" stresses dwelling to enjoy, "ground" holding and growing merits; Miào Jìng: holding the bodhisattva's boundless merits within is "ground"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "abode" emphasises enjoying a dwelling; "ground" emphasises holding and growing the bodhisattva's merits. Venerable Miào Jìng: it holds the bodhisattva's boundless merits — hence "ground."
